title: Depth-aware machine learning for 3D reconstruction of fibrous porous electrodes from FIB-SEM tomography
summary: An annotation-free framework combining monocular depth estimation (trained on macroscale images) with unsupervised clustering separates in-plane polymer cross-sections from subsurface contributions in FIB-SEM tomography. On copper-coated electrospun PVDF-HFP fiber mats it preserves fiber morphology better than conventional supervised and unsupervised segmentation, with improved agreement on pore diameter, fiber volume ratio and Cu depth decrease. Validation used capillary flow porometry, pycnometry and wide-angle X-ray tomography on a single material system.
ai_technology: Depth-aware machine learning: monocular depth estimation plus unsupervised clustering
organization: ETH Zurich; EPFL; Empa; European Synchrotron Radiation Facility

evidence.tested: Reconstructions of copper-coated electrospun PVDF-HFP fiber mats compared with conventional segmentation and with independent measurements (porometry, pycnometry, wide-angle X-ray CT).
evidence.unknown: Generalisation beyond the tested fiber mat system is not stated in the reviewed material.
evidence.ai_role: Monocular depth estimation model, trained on macroscale images, plus unsupervised clustering to separate in-plane from subsurface material in FIB-SEM slices.
